lessons.title: Backup architecture and trusted recovery by design
lessons.body:
## Design the service that must return
Backup design starts from a recoverable service, not a file-copy schedule. Identify the functions that must return, their minimum acceptable operating state, the data or controller state that may be lost, and the time available. A historian service can require current acquisition, retained alarm history, user roles, trusted device identities and useful timestamps. A controller service can require approved logic, supported firmware, I/O configuration, retained values, current physical permissives and an authorized commissioning sequence. Restoring an executable alone does not restore either service.

Define recovery point objective and recovery time objective against those outcomes. RPO limits loss of required recoverable data or state; it is not automatically equal to the scheduled backup interval. If the newest usable consistent point is older because later jobs failed, that usable point governs the current recovery claim. RTO measures the declared interval from disruption to the specified service acceptance. Include retrieval, credentials, licences, staging, restoration, data reconciliation and required functional/security checks where they occur within that interval. Report partial service separately if operators receive live values before history and other required functions return.

## Define consistency sets and restoration units
List the objects that must form a compatible set. An application can require executable version, database schema, configuration, plugins, trust store and service identities. A PLC can require project, libraries, engineering tool, firmware, hardware mapping, task configuration and a documented retained-state policy. Files copied at different instants may each be readable but collectively inconsistent. Use a supported application-aware backup, quiesced snapshot, transactional mechanism or other justified method that preserves the relevant consistency boundary.

A crash-consistent image records a storage state but does not automatically establish application-consistent recovery. The application may need its own recovery logs and supported replay procedure. A filesystem snapshot also does not capture an external licence server, directory role or controller force table unless those objects are explicitly included. Define what the snapshot includes, what it references and what must be reconstructed independently. Test the actual vendor-supported mechanism on a representative baseline instead of assuming that all products interpret snapshots identically.

Full, differential and incremental schemes trade capture cost, storage and restore dependencies. State the chain precisely. An incremental set commonly depends on the base and every required intervening increment; a missing link can make later data unusable. A differential set normally depends on its base and the selected differential, but exact product semantics still need verification. Transaction-log replay also requires the correct starting checkpoint, a continuous required log sequence and supported target selection. A recent archive timestamp does not repair a missing earlier log segment.

Create a manifest for each restoration unit. Include asset/service identity, capture point and time basis, object versions, consistency method, required predecessor sets, key identifiers, integrity/provenance references, supported restore tool and applicable test evidence. The following is an illustrative structure, not a vendor command:

```json
{
  "service": "BMS-A",
  "application": "4.0",
  "schema": "4",
  "checkpoint": "C100",
  "required_log_range": [101, 118],
  "trust_reference": "offline-release-register-7",
  "identity_reconciliation": "current-authority-register",
  "physical_handback": "approved-controller-sequence"
}
```

A manifest makes dependencies inspectable; it does not itself prove that the listed files exist or restore correctly. Validate the objects, then perform representative restoration and record actual results.

## Separate availability, integrity, confidentiality and independence
Replication, redundancy and backup solve overlapping but different problems. A live replica can improve continuity while promptly copying accidental deletion, encrypted files or a harmful configuration. Recovery needs suitable historical states and a trust boundary that the initiating incident cannot trivially destroy. Analyze administrative reach, key custody, storage write/delete authority, network access and retention enforcement. Two appliances under one unrestricted account are not independent merely because they have different names.

Offline or immutable copies can reduce particular alteration paths. They do not guarantee clean content, correct capture, usable keys or an executable restoration procedure. A locked copy captured after compromise faithfully preserves the compromised state. An immutable retention period also has capacity and lifecycle effects: legitimate old data may remain undeletable until its policy permits removal. Design retention, storage headroom and authorized administration together; do not assume an emergency administrator can always shorten an enforced retention lock.

Hashes establish byte equality relative to a reference. If an attacker can replace both the image and its adjacent hash file, that equality has a weak trust basis. Use appropriately protected references, authenticated provenance and independent evidence. A valid signature depends on the signing authority and its state at the relevant time; a later key-compromise advisory can change the assessment. Confidentiality needs encryption and access control where required, but recovery staff must be able to retrieve keys through a controlled path that survives the modeled outage.

Identify bootstrap cycles explicitly. A vault that authenticates only through a directory cannot be the sole store for that directory's recovery credential without an independent recovery mechanism. Provide organizational custody, scoped emergency access, evidence of use and post-use reconciliation. Do not solve the cycle by publishing every secret or disabling all protection. Include absence of the normal administrator and loss of the usual workstation in appropriate drills.

## Engineer order, concurrency and resource contention
Construct a directed dependency graph. A task can start only after its prerequisites and required resources are available. With genuinely independent resources, parallel branches finish according to the longest relevant path, not the sum of every task. For example, network restoration may precede identity recovery; then application and controller work can proceed in parallel before integrated acceptance. If both branches require one exclusive licensed workstation, their nominal parallelism disappears.

Record durations as estimates or measurements with the correct label. An optimistic vendor demonstration that excludes activation and physical handback is not a measured site RTO. Test retrieval from the intended storage tier and location, the availability of tools and entitlements, and the time needed to reconstruct a catalogue. A surviving backup medium may still be unusable if its required catalogue database or encryption key is lost. Design alternatives according to the actual product capabilities.

## Restore current trust, not every historical privilege
Historical restoration must be reconciled with current approved authority. Remove or replace revoked accounts, old CA trust, exposed keys, temporary firewall rules and obsolete endpoints. Restore necessary current service identities deliberately. Replaying the entire old account database can reauthorize a departed supplier; deleting every identity can prevent the service from working. Compare intended current roles against restored effective permissions and test both required access and denied old authority.

Use three connected acceptance paths. Network/platform checks cover routing, segmentation, management accounts, automation and independent BMC or firmware state. Controller/engineering checks cover compatible project loading, I/O and task configuration, forces, modes, retained commands and physical feedback under qualified authority. Supervisory/data checks cover point mapping, quality/freshness, alarms, historian consistency and current trust relationships. A clean OS image does not establish BMC trust, and a matching PLC project does not prove an old force is absent.

## Validate recovery without inventing evidence
Define a representative failure scenario and unavailable dependencies before the drill. Preserve provenance of the selected source and explain why it is believed suitable. Execute the supported restoration in an authorized environment, record elapsed stages and deviations, and test normal function, prohibited authority, degraded behavior and future backup readiness. Keep raw observations where appropriate. Recovered historical samples retain source times and quality; interpolation and estimates must remain distinguishable from actual measurements.

A design may provide an offline analytical plan before equipment is available, but that plan remains a design artifact. Mark unexecuted steps clearly and retain vendor, representative-hardware and physical commissioning gates. A failed drill is useful evidence when it exposes a dependency, leads to a controlled correction and is retested. The original failure should remain visible rather than being rewritten as a pass after the procedure improves.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.scenario: SYNTHETIC CASE — SYNTHETIC RECOVERY DESIGN: Service fails at 15:00; required RPO is 15 minutes and RTO is 105 minutes to integrated accepted operation. B1 is an independently protected, application-consistent 14:32 backup containing application 4.0/schema 4. B2 was captured at 14:55 after an unreviewed privileged startup task appeared at 14:48; B2 is immutable but its trust is unresolved. A separate file copy combines database pages at checkpoint C100 with logs beginning at C110, omitting C101–C109. Incremental chain I0→I1→I2→I3 is required by its declared restore format, but I2 is missing. Image X and its matching hash file are both writable by the production administrator. The live replica faithfully copies deletions. Backup decryption material is inside a vault that requires directory authentication; the directory recovery credential is only in that vault. Independently controlled bootstrap access has not yet been designed. Network restore takes 15 minutes, then identity takes 20. After identity, application restore takes 40 and controller restore 35; with independent qualified staff and tools those branches can run concurrently. Integrated acceptance then takes 20. A proposed cost reduction leaves one exclusive licensed workstation for both branches. B1 contains supplier-old, revoked at 14:50, and lacks service-new approved at 14:52. The controller project matches approval, but an old runtime force holds a permissive true. The host OS is clean, while BMC firmware/key trust is unknown. Application 3.0 cannot read schema 4. The backup catalogue is required by the selected restore product and is stored only on the failed primary server. Buffered genuine historian samples are available with original source timestamps; other gap values can only be estimated. Retention lock L prevents deletion for 90 days and does not permit shortening by the campaign administrator.
worked_examples.solution:
B1 represents 28 minutes of lost recoverable state at 15:00, so it does not meet the 15-minute RPO by itself. B2's recency and immutability do not establish a clean state. The checkpoint/log gap and missing I2 each break their own declared restoration chain. Image X's adjacent hash is not an independent reference when the same authority can change both.

The dependency plan is blocked until a controlled bootstrap path and the required catalogue are available. Once those prerequisites are genuinely resolved, the stated independent-resource critical path is 15+20+max(40,35)+20=95 minutes, within 105. One exclusive workstation serializes the two branches and gives 15+20+40+35+20=130 minutes, so that proposed saving changes feasibility. These are synthetic planning calculations, not measured field results.

Recovery must remove supplier-old, add service-new through current authorization, inspect and clear the inappropriate runtime force under the approved controls procedure, and establish the separate BMC trust state. Rolling only the application executable back to 3.0 would not make schema 4 compatible. Retain genuine buffered samples with their source times and mark estimates as derived. Capacity planning must respect the actual 90-day retention lock rather than assuming the campaign administrator can delete copies early. Accept required function and denied authority across platform, controller and supervisory paths.

guided_practice.prompt: Draw the restore dependency graph, calculate the independent-resource and single-workstation completion times, and identify the conditions that still prevent either calculation from becoming an accepted recovery claim.
guided_practice.hint: The graph is not executable until bootstrap, catalogue, trust and current-authority prerequisites are resolved; arithmetic alone does not supply them.
guided_practice.solution: Independent resources give a 95-minute critical path; one exclusive workstation gives 130 minutes. Both assume the specified durations and available prerequisites. The unresolved bootstrap cycle, lost catalogue, source selection, identity reconciliation, runtime force, BMC trust and physical acceptance require explicit design and evidence. B1 alone also misses RPO by 13 minutes because its recoverable point is 28 minutes old.

independent_task.brief: Produce a versioned recovery design for a supported representative OT service: consistency manifest, copy/retention and administrative-independence architecture, bootstrap/key custody, dependency/resource schedule, three-path acceptance matrix and a bounded drill plan. Execute only the authorized local or representative portions and label remaining steps not performed.
deliverables: An evidence table distinguishing supplied facts, assumptions and unknowns.
A technically reasoned decision and a reproducible verification or validation procedure.
acceptance_criteria: The design distinguishes a usable recovery point from a job schedule and a complete service RTO from image-copy time.
Consistency chains, protected provenance, key/catalogue dependencies and shared administrative/resource causes are explicit.
Current authority, controller runtime state, platform trust and operational data semantics are verified or retained as named open gates.
Synthetic estimates, actual local outputs and unperformed vendor/physical tests are clearly separated.
independent_task.limitations: Synthetic analytical work only. No real device, process safety claim, vendor command execution, standard conformance determination or credential is implied.

lessons.title: Configuration automation, guarded changes and partial-failure recovery
lessons.body:
## Model the change before choosing its transport
Automation is an engineered state transition. Identify the controlled objects, their current effective state, the required state, who authorizes the difference and what operating conditions must remain true. A configuration file in a repository is desired state. A prepared candidate is proposed state. An accepted running configuration is active configuration. The observed service and physical process are additional states whose behavior must be checked. These can disagree: a successful upload may not activate a candidate, an active configuration may disappear after reboot, and a correct configuration may operate against a failed sensor.

Create stable object identities and explicit ownership. Use an asset identifier and verified device identity instead of relying on an address that may be reassigned. For a rule, use a unique managed rule identifier and defined position or ordering relationship. Distinguish objects fully managed by the automation from objects another authorized process maintains. A blanket replacement of an entire rule list can erase a legitimate rule outside the automation's ownership. Conversely, an additive script can leave obsolete permissive rules in place indefinitely. Reconciliation must deliberately create, update and remove objects within a declared boundary.

Compute a semantic difference. Some collections are sets; other lists have order-dependent meaning. Sorting an ordered first-match firewall policy can change access even if its set of rule strings remains identical. A string comparison can also report harmless formatting as a change or miss effective inherited settings outside the file. The planning stage should interpret the relevant schema, defaults, references, order and dependencies. Unsupported or ambiguous input must produce an explicit unresolved finding rather than an invented value.

## Derive idempotence and its limits
For a defined configuration state s and an operation f, idempotence means f(f(s)) = f(s). State what the equality includes. Appending a new duplicate rule on every run fails this property. Replacing the value of a uniquely identified managed rule with the same desired value can satisfy it for that configuration projection. Operational side effects require separate analysis. A client that reloads a gateway on every no-change run may converge to the same policy while repeatedly interrupting telemetry. An operation can also be repeatable and consistently install an unauthorized or unsafe rule. Idempotence is useful for retries; it does not establish authority, correctness or operational safety.

Implement a no-change path. Read the relevant effective state, normalize only where semantics permit it, compute the delta, and avoid mutation when no authorized change remains. Test both the first application and a second application. The first should perform the intended transformation. The second should produce no additional managed objects or unnecessary disruptive action. Record the chosen comparison boundary so an audit-event timestamp or unrelated dynamic counter does not cause an endless rewrite loop.

## Bind the plan to its inputs and assumptions
A reviewable plan is more than a list of commands. Include target identities, observed revisions, desired artifact digest, renderer and schema versions, dependency order, required privileges, expected differences, preconditions, verification steps and recovery choices. Preserve the exact immutable plan reviewed. If an engineer approves an artifact generated from template T7 and someone changes T7 before application, the old approval does not automatically authorize the newly rendered payload. Regenerate and review the changed plan or use a controlled approval mechanism that explicitly covers the permitted variation.

Separate observation from decision and execution. The following original pseudocode describes a bounded workflow, not a command that is safe to run on arbitrary products:

```text
observed = read_verified_targets()
plan = derive_semantic_delta(observed, versioned_desired_inputs)
validate_schema_and_owned_scope(plan)
review(plan.digest, plan.target_identities, plan.expected_revisions)
for bounded_stage in plan.dependency_order:
    recheck_operational_preconditions(bounded_stage)
    apply_using_supported_revision_guard(bounded_stage)
    persist_each_target_outcome(success, failed, unknown, skipped)
    reconcile_unknowns_and_verify_required_behavior()
    advance_only_when_stage_acceptance_is_met()
```

A dry run can expose a proposed difference, but it does not prove that every later permission, device response or service condition will match the prediction. Test what the tool's dry-run mode actually evaluates. Some providers calculate changes locally; others call remote validation; neither is equivalent to executing and accepting the resulting service.

## Prevent stale writes and unsafe retries
Where an HTTP configuration API supports revision tags, a specific strong ETag with If-Match can bind an update to the representation that was reviewed. A wildcard condition checks existence instead of that particular revision. Neither condition authenticates the caller or establishes process readiness. A failed revision check requires fresh observation and a new decision; blindly removing the condition defeats its purpose. RFC 9110 also distinguishes idempotent request semantics from arbitrary application commands. A lost response does not prove that a command was never accepted.

Classify outcomes explicitly. Success means the stated operation has sufficient positive evidence. Failure means its defined failure condition is established. Unknown means evidence cannot yet distinguish relevant outcomes. Skipped means the operation was not attempted, for example because an earlier dependency failed. A transport timeout can produce an unknown outcome. Before retrying a non-repeatable action, query a supported operation record or authoritative current state. An application-provided idempotency token can help only if its documented lifetime, scope and result behavior cover this operation. Inventing a client request label does not make an unsupported server deduplicate requests.

## Use supported device transactions without inventing global atomicity
Discover device capabilities before constructing a workflow. NETCONF candidate, validation, confirmed commit and startup persistence are distinct capabilities and operations. A supported candidate workflow can stage a change before activation. Confirmed commit provides a timed return to the earlier configuration unless properly confirmed; it does not undo physical effects that happened while the new configuration operated. Saving an accepted running configuration for restart is a separate concern where a startup datastore is used. Apply the protocol's actual lock and session rules, and test the supported implementation on the target baseline.

A collection of per-device transactions is not automatically one atomic transaction. If gateway A changes and gateway B rejects its change, the system can remain in a mixed state. Design a dependency graph and safe intermediate states. For telemetry-path migration, a justified sequence can establish and verify the new path, move the consumer, verify the resulting service, and then remove the obsolete authority. The details depend on whether temporary overlap is permitted. Some systems require a bounded interruption instead. State that choice and its operating constraints; a generic instruction to add everything before removing anything can create unauthorized overlap.

A lock has a scope: datastore, object set, session, duration and participating writers. Confirm which writers and interfaces it actually excludes. A lock on one device does not protect a second device or freeze a changing pump permissive. Revision guards protect configured state only to their documented boundary. Recheck live operational predicates such as healthy standby, approved mode, current maintenance window and available recovery access near the dependent action. If these conditions change during execution, halt at the defined safe point and follow the approved exception or recovery procedure.

## Bound failure impact and design compensation
Choose concurrency from shared limits and failure consequences. A service account rate limit, a narrow management link, one recovery operator or the need to keep one redundant gateway available can constrain parallelism. A representative canary reduces exposure and supplies evidence about its tested conditions; it does not prove compatibility for an untested model, firmware branch, failover mode or process condition. Segment a rollout by meaningful compatibility and operational boundaries and define a stop threshold before observing the results.

Rollback is another controlled change. Establish which prior state remains compatible with current data and authority. An old application may not read a database schema introduced during deployment. A stored prior configuration may revive revoked access. Removing a newly added telemetry route does not recover missed samples, and reverting a controller configuration does not reverse an already completed physical action. Design the relevant remedy: exact supported restoration, a tested compensating change, forward correction, data reconciliation, or a controlled service hold. Verify the remedy and retain partial-failure records. Do not label every recovery action a successful rollback.

Automation must also protect its own authority. Keep deployment credentials out of source, plan output and ordinary logs; use controlled secret references and record an appropriate identity or key identifier. A read-only evidence collector should not share the deployer's write role merely for convenience. Treat inventory notes, imported descriptions and device-returned text as data. Validate typed fields and use structured interfaces rather than executing arbitrary strings as shell fragments. An approved inventory entry is not an approval for a command hidden inside its free-text description.

## Close on observed service, security and persistence
Define acceptance before application. Check the active revision through an appropriate fresh read, then check required service behavior and prohibited behavior at the relevant boundary. Include denied stale identities, intended flow limits, alarm delivery, data quality and necessary failover checks. A cached desired-state view can repeat the approved revision while the target still runs the old one. Preserve the observation time, target identity, query method and uncertainty. Confirm restart persistence using an approved representative method where required; a production reboot is not a routine substitute for designing the test.

The final record should connect approved intent, actual attempts, per-target outcomes, reconciled state, acceptance results and unresolved gates. A scheduler's green exit status is not sufficient if the child tool swallowed a failed request or skipped a target. Use explicit result contracts and propagate failures and unknowns. A lesson exercise can implement this state machine against local synthetic files and mock responses. Label its evidence as local simulation; target protocol interoperability, physical service behavior and production timing remain separate validation tasks until actually performed.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.scenario:
SYNTHETIC CASE — Automation design exercise: all assets, requests and results are synthetic.

Managed service: gateways A and B carry required EPMS telemetry. Exactly one healthy gateway must remain available during the staged change. The approved plan P7 targets A identity cert-A, observed configuration revision "r17", desired policy H7, renderer T7 and a declared maintenance window. While P7 awaits execution, another approved change advances A to "r18" and the template is edited to T8. The mock HTTP API uses strong tags and returns 412 without mutation when a supplied specific If-Match tag mismatches. If-Match: * succeeds on the existence condition whenever the configuration resource exists.

Two proposed clients: APPEND adds a fresh rule object every run; SET updates one uniquely identified managed rule to its desired value. SET's current wrapper reloads A on every run, even when the semantic delta is empty. A policy list is first-match: an attempted alphabetical sort places DENY-ALL before PERMIT-EPMS although the set of rule strings is unchanged. Read-only collector C and deployer D currently share D's write credential. An imported inventory note contains a shell command; it is free text, not an approved operation.

Staging observations: an earlier health sample reports B healthy at 10:00, but live B status becomes unhealthy at 10:08 before A's 10:10 disruption. The canary used gateway model X and firmware 3; the next group includes model Y firmware 5. A supported migration permits temporary overlap only for the two named telemetry endpoints, then requires old-path removal after consumer cutover and verification.

Device A advertises candidate, validation, confirmed-commit and startup support. Device B advertises no candidate capability. A's candidate lock covers its supported local datastore, not B or plant status. A temporarily activates a new configuration under a 120-second confirmed-commit timer; required end-to-end telemetry tests have not yet passed. Its accepted running configuration has not been copied to its separate startup datastore.

Failure records: A reports its local change succeeded; B rejects its change. Separately, a POST /operations/failover request times out after transmission. In this mock API every accepted POST starts another failover sequence; the API offers an operation-status record but does not deduplicate repeated requests. The orchestrator reports the timeout as unknown, not failed. The old application A3 cannot read schema S4 created by the new application A4. A stored prior access configuration contains supplier-old, whose authority is now revoked. A dashboard displays cached desired revision H7 without a fresh device read. A proposed completion log stores full bearer tokens and only the scheduler's exit code, with no per-target outcomes.
worked_examples.solution:
P7 cannot be applied unchanged as a current approved transition. A's revision and the rendering input changed. Read the current identified target, derive the semantic delta using the intended versioned input and obtain approval for that concrete plan. Under the stated mock API, If-Match "r17" against "r18" returns 412 without mutation; replacing it with a wildcard would remove the exact-version protection.

APPEND is not idempotent because another application creates another managed rule. SET can be idempotent for the defined rule value, but its unconditional reload creates an unnecessary operational disruption. Add a semantic no-change path. Preserve first-match policy order: moving DENY-ALL above the required permit blocks the flow despite equal rule membership. Separate C's read authority from D's deployment role and parse the inventory note as data.

The 10:00 standby observation is stale for the 10:10 disruption. B's current failure violates the declared one-healthy-gateway invariant, so hold A's disruptive stage and follow the approved recovery or exception process. Model X firmware 3 does not establish compatibility for model Y firmware 5. The migration must limit temporary overlap to its named endpoints, prove the new path, move the consumer, verify service and remove obsolete authority.

A's capabilities permit its particular candidate workflow; B requires a separately justified supported method. A's lock does not create a cross-device transaction or freeze plant health. Do not confirm A merely because the timer is running: required acceptance has not passed. Use the planned bounded acceptance or return procedure. After a genuinely accepted change, address the distinct startup-persistence requirement. A-success/B-reject remains a mixed result requiring reconciliation and an approved next action.

The timed-out failover command is unknown. Query the supported operation record and current state before deciding whether another action is needed. An immediate duplicate POST could start a second sequence. Reinstalling A3 over S4 is an incompatible remedy, while restoring the old access configuration would revive revoked authority. Select and verify supported compensation. Fresh effective-state and service evidence must replace the cached desired view. Completion logs must omit usable credentials and include target outcomes, uncertainties and acceptance results rather than only the scheduler status.

guided_practice.prompt: Construct a state table for P7 with rows for revision drift, template drift, lost POST response, A-success/B-reject, standby failure and confirmed-commit acceptance. For each, state observed facts, allowed next action and evidence needed before advancing.
guided_practice.hint: Keep authorization, configuration revision, process health and transport outcome as separate dimensions. A green result in one dimension does not settle the others.
guided_practice.solution: Revision drift and template drift require a newly derived reviewable plan; the timeout requires outcome reconciliation; the mixed deployment requires a per-target recovery decision; standby failure blocks the disruptive step; an unaccepted temporary commit must follow the bounded verification or return path. Record exact target identity, input revisions and fresh observations for every decision.

independent_task.brief: Design an offline change executor using local JSON fixtures and mock API responses. Implement immutable plan input references, semantic difference, explicit success/failed/unknown/skipped outcomes, an operational-precondition gate, a retry decision and an acceptance report. Include fixtures for no change, stale revision, changed renderer, response loss, partial device failure, lost standby and incompatible compensation. Do not connect to a real OT endpoint.
deliverables: An evidence table distinguishing supplied facts, assumptions and unknowns.
A technically reasoned decision and a reproducible verification or validation procedure.
acceptance_criteria: A second no-change run produces no extra managed objects and no modeled reload.
Stale revision, changed input and unhealthy standby fixtures stop at their distinct declared gates.
The lost-response fixture remains unknown until a supplied authoritative operation observation resolves it; no automatic duplicate failover occurs.
Partial results and incompatible restoration are preserved as distinct findings; the final report distinguishes simulated results from unperformed target and physical validation.
independent_task.limitations: Synthetic analytical work only. No real device, process safety claim, vendor command execution, standard conformance determination or credential is implied.

lessons.title: CFAT planning: requirements, test oracles and representative failure conditions
lessons.body:
### Turn a requirement into an observable decision

A cybersecurity factory acceptance test examines the integrated design before site deployment, using a controlled representation of the intended installation. Its useful output is a defensible statement about a particular requirement on a particular baseline under recorded conditions. A product demonstration can show that a feature exists; acceptance testing asks whether the assembled configuration satisfies the owner’s requirement, including the conditions in which it must deny an action, preserve a function or recover. Factory evidence cannot silently substitute for site dependencies that the factory did not reproduce.

Rewrite vague statements before constructing tests. “Remote access is secure” cannot produce a repeatable pass decision. A testable requirement identifies a principal and role, permitted target, operation, activation condition, expiry, required record and failure response. For example, an approved maintenance identity may read gateway diagnostics during a bounded support session; a project-changing operation requires a separate authorized role. The test needs a permitted read and a relevant forbidden write, using the intended identity path. Successfully opening a remote desktop proves neither permission boundary nor downstream attribution.

For each requirement, build a trace from requirement identifier to design mechanism, configuration artifact, test stimulus, expected observations, result and retained evidence. The test oracle is the rule that decides whether the observations satisfy the requirement. Fix it before execution. If the operator changes a threshold after seeing a failure, that is a proposed requirement change, requiring a justified approval and impact review. It is not merely correction of a test report. Retain both the original expectation and the approved revised baseline where a legitimate change occurs.

### Build the test unit and its observations

A repeatable test case contains an identifier, purpose, initial conditions, authorized participants, baseline identities, stimulus, observation points, expected results, permitted uncertainty, stop conditions, restoration method and evidence destination. Preconditions are executable checks: a default-deny rule is actually active, the intended user has no inherited administrator group, clocks have the recorded accuracy, a simulator is isolated, and temporary bypasses have known state. An unchecked precondition can make a passing result irrelevant. For example, testing a forbidden operation against an unreachable controller does not demonstrate authorization enforcement.

Separate the stimulus from the oracle where practicable. An automation tool that sends an API request and declares success from its own request log only confirms intent. Observe the effective target state, application response and relevant process consequence through an appropriate independent channel. For a rejected write, preserve the attempted identity and target, the denial at the enforcement point, and evidence that the controlled value did not change. For a permitted read, compare returned identity, value, unit, quality and age against the synthetic source. A number that looks reasonable can still represent the wrong point.

Negative tests need a working path and a relevant forbidden action. First demonstrate that the authorized diagnostic read can traverse the path. Then use the deliberately limited identity to attempt a bounded forbidden operation in the isolated fixture. This discriminates authorization denial from absent connectivity. Vary the principal or operation according to the requirement; indiscriminately scanning every port is not a substitute for a designed test. Record cleanup because test accounts, permissive rules and bypass tokens can otherwise survive as new exposure.

### Cover states, boundaries and interactions

Build coverage across requirement, operating mode and fault condition. Normal operation, startup, planned maintenance, failover, loss of a shared service and recovery may use different code paths and authorities. A primary firewall’s correct rule does not establish that the standby received it. An identity service outage may activate cached credentials or emergency access. A source outage may freeze the last good measurement while the network remains connected. Select tests that challenge these mechanisms, rather than accumulating unrelated passing checks.

Boundary values reveal comparison and timing errors. For a requirement that marks information stale when age is greater than five seconds, an age of exactly five seconds and one just above it have different expected results. State how timestamps are generated, where age is measured and what clock error is allowed. If the test requires a 200 ms response and measurement uncertainty is ±40 ms, a recorded 190 ms is not a confident pass under a conservative upper-bound rule. The plan must state its decision rule in advance; rounding away uncertainty is not evidence.

Not every combination can be executed. Explain the selection using risk, distinct mechanisms and equivalence arguments. Reusing one test across identical instances is defensible only when relevant hardware, software, configuration, dependencies and fault behavior really are equivalent. Preserve exceptions. High-consequence or structurally different paths deserve direct evidence. Coverage percentages should count applicable requirements and distinguish passed, failed, blocked, not tested and formally excluded states. A blocked test is not a pass, and removing it from the denominator must not manufacture readiness.

### Specify representative equipment and safe constraints

The fixture description identifies supported product and software versions, topology, policy, identities, data mappings, load, dependencies and simulated physical interfaces. A simulator can validate state-machine logic and protocol handling but cannot prove actual cable routing, actuator travel time, electrical independence or physical sensor calibration. Assign these remaining claims to site or physical acceptance tests with the responsible qualified owner. State exactly which factory conclusions remain valid after a changed firmware, addressing scheme or dependency.

Plan fault injection with the process owner and test authority. Define permitted stimuli, bounded intensity, expected containment, observers and abort triggers. Use isolated fixtures for destructive or disruptive cases; do not reproduce a risky stimulus on live plant because it succeeded in a simulator. Determine the restored state before starting. The test should finish with required protection effective, temporary accounts removed, baseline artifacts reconciled and evidence saved. Stop authority must be usable by the participant observing an unsafe or out-of-scope condition, not buried behind a distant approval queue.

### Construct a practical test schedule

Sequence readiness checks before dependent tests. Establish instrumentation and time quality, verify target identity, prove the authorized path, challenge excess authority, introduce one controlled dependency fault, verify the specified degraded response, restore and rerun the affected positive/negative checks. Some observations can run concurrently; changes that alter another test’s preconditions cannot. Reserve time for evidence review and restoration, not just stimulus execution. A campaign that finishes its last fault injection at the end of the booked window has no demonstrated recovery margin.

The acceptance plan should make unresolved conditions visible to procurement and operations. State what the factory can prove, what must be witnessed at site, who can disposition a deviation, and which failures block shipment or service introduction. This is how a requirements specification becomes a usable engineering control rather than a document attached after the design is already fixed.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.scenario: SYNTHETIC CASE — Factory fixture F7 contains gateway G, a limited support identity R, controller simulator C and an independent historian observer H. Baseline: gateway firmware 4.2, policy P12, point map M8. Requirement A: R may read diagnostics but cannot write a setpoint. Requirement B: source age strictly greater than 5.0 s must display stale and inhibit supervisory writes; exactly 5.0 s remains valid. Requirement C: prohibited attempts are attributable to identity and target. Requirement D: after policy failover, the same A/B/C conditions hold. The factory substitutes local accounts for the future site directory and uses a simulator in place of physical I/O. Proposed tests: T1 login succeeds; T2 read returns expected value; T3 write times out while C is disconnected; T4 source age 4.9 s; T5 active gateway fails over but no limited-role operation is repeated; T6 response measured 190 ms with ±40 ms uncertainty against a 200 ms maximum using a conservative upper-bound rule. There are 12 applicable acceptance requirements: 8 passed, 2 failed, 1 blocked, 1 not tested. A proposed report removes the blocked and untested requirements and reports 80% acceptance.
worked_examples.solution:
T1 is entry authentication evidence, while T2 provides one positive diagnostic operation. T3 cannot distinguish authorization denial from the disconnected target: reconnect the isolated simulator, prove a permitted read, attempt the bounded forbidden write and observe both the denial and unchanged simulated setpoint. T4 leaves the stale transition and exact equality untested; test 5.0 s and a controlled age just above 5.0 s as well. T5 demonstrates a transition but not preservation of the role, stale-data and attribution requirements on the surviving policy instance.

For T6 the conservative upper bound is 190 + 40 = 230 ms, so the result cannot establish the 200 ms maximum. It is not proof that the actual mechanism necessarily exceeded 200 ms; reduce uncertainty or improve the response and repeat under the approved rule. Eight of twelve applicable requirements are evidenced as passed, or 66.7%; the other states must remain visible. The 80% figure describes eight passed out of ten executed tests, not acceptance of twelve requirements. Directory integration and physical I/O behavior remain site/physical obligations because those dependencies were substituted in F7.

guided_practice.prompt: Rewrite T3 and T5 into bounded tests with initial state, stimulus, independent observations, oracle and cleanup. Calculate T6’s upper bound and report requirement status without hiding blocked work.
guided_practice.hint: A denied write needs a functioning path. A failover test must repeat the invariant checks on the surviving state. Compare measured value plus uncertainty with the stated upper limit.
guided_practice.solution: Establish C reachable and the approved R identity effective; demonstrate a read, then attempt the simulated setpoint write and require an attributable denial plus unchanged value. After approved gateway failover, repeat read, forbidden write, stale-source behavior and attribution on the surviving instance. Restore the fixture and remove temporary identities. The timing bound is 230 ms; 8/12 = 66.7% passed, with 2 failed, 1 blocked and 1 not tested retained separately.

independent_task.brief: Create a factory acceptance plan for an isolated EPMS/BMS gateway fixture: six test cases covering permitted use, prohibited use, stale input, identity loss, failover and restoration. Include one explicit factory-to-site evidence limitation.
deliverables: An evidence table distinguishing supplied facts, assumptions and unknowns.
A technically reasoned decision and a reproducible verification or validation procedure.
acceptance_criteria: Every test traces an observable decision to a requirement and exact baseline.
Negative tests distinguish unavailable communication from enforced denial.
Timing and boundary operators are explicit, and blocked/not-tested states remain visible.
The plan contains stop conditions, restoration checks and deferred physical/site obligations.
independent_task.limitations: Synthetic analytical work only. No real device, process safety claim, vendor command execution, standard conformance determination or credential is implied.

lessons.title: CFAT execution: distinguish policy defects, stale state and misleading success signals
lessons.body:
### Establish what is actually running

Execution starts by checking the approved fixture against reality. Record the active software, loaded project, effective policy, role membership, source mappings and instrumentation. A candidate configuration stored on disk is different from a configuration loaded by the device. An API’s successful transport response can contain an operation-level error, and an accepted asynchronous job can fail later. Treat each boundary explicitly: request constructed, request received, candidate validated, task executed, effective state changed, intended behavior observed. Evidence at one stage does not automatically close later stages.

Use the smallest observation that distinguishes competing causes. Suppose a forbidden write succeeds. Potential explanations include an excessively broad rule, a wrong identity group, an old established session, a bypass path, an unactivated candidate, or a test aimed at a different asset. Capture the principal, exact destination and operation, then inspect the effective enforcement point and corresponding result. Changing several controls simultaneously may produce a passing retest while leaving the cause unknown. It also makes rollback and regression scope harder to justify.

### Diagnose authorization in the path that performed the operation

For an ordered first-match rule set, evaluate the actual packet against each active rule in order. A broad allow above a specific deny can make the deny unreachable for that traffic. The existence of the deny in an exported configuration is therefore not sufficient. Confirm whether the export is active, inspect meaningful hit counters, and correlate a fresh test transaction with a controlled capture or operation log. The interpretation depends on product behavior: some rule engines use different ordering or policy stages, so preserve the selected platform’s supported semantics in a real test.

Stateful sessions introduce a second time dimension. The policy used to create a session may differ from the candidate later committed. Whether an existing session is reevaluated or terminated depends on the platform and operation. A session that remains usable after a rule edit does not alone prove a fresh session could be created. Conversely, a new session’s denial does not prove previously authorized sessions were revoked. If the requirement covers immediate withdrawal of authority, test both conditions using the supported, approved session lifecycle. Do not clear all production sessions merely to obtain a cleaner experiment.

Application permission differs from network reachability. A TCP connection and a successful encrypted handshake establish only their respective communication and trust properties. A permitted industrial read does not establish that writes are restricted. For encrypted application traffic, an observation point that cannot decrypt or interpret the operation cannot certify command-level enforcement from port counters alone. Use application authorization results, trusted target state and appropriately bounded server records to prove the operation’s consequence.

### Validate data meaning, age and effective action

An observed value has an identity, unit, quality, timestamp and relationship to a physical or simulated source. Test each property that the requirement relies on. A gateway may return the last good number after a source fails; a smooth value then demonstrates cache availability, not current measurement validity. For a design that inhibits writes on bad quality or excessive age, the gate should combine those conditions. Checking age alone can accept a recent value explicitly marked invalid, while checking quality alone can accept a very old value.

This illustrative gate operates only on a synthetic fixture whose sample and current time share a validated monotonic time base:

```python
def usable(sample, now, maximum_age):
    age = now - sample['sample_time']
    return (sample['quality'] == 'good'
            and 0 <= age <= maximum_age)
```

The lower bound rejects impossible future samples under this model. A production implementation must define timestamp authority, uncertainty, rollover behavior and acceptable synchronization loss; blindly subtracting unrelated wall clocks is not equivalent. This gate is a decision model, not a field controller program or a safety function.

Separate command acceptance from achieved state. A response may acknowledge that a request entered a queue while the target rejects it or the actuator never reaches position. Observe the agreed feedback within the required interval and apply the specified failure response. In the factory simulator, log requested state and simulated achieved state separately. In the installed plant, use the approved point and qualified test authority. A setpoint echo generated from the request buffer is not independent confirmation of the controlled quantity.

### Preserve measurement validity during failure injection

Instrumentation can fail before the system under test. A capture filtered for the wrong VLAN can show no packets even while the operation succeeds. A saturated collector can lose the very alarms the test intends to count. A clock correction can reverse apparent event order. Check capture placement, filter, direction, time basis, drop counters and synchronization before attributing an absence to the tested control. If the observation chain is inadequate, classify the result as inconclusive or blocked, correct the instrumentation and repeat; do not turn missing evidence into a pass.

For a conservation check, compare the number of uniquely identified events generated with the number received, allowing for explicitly defined duplicates, batching and interval boundaries. If 1,000 unique source events were expected and 995 matching events arrived after the full permitted delivery interval, five remain unaccounted for. The loss fraction is 5/1,000 = 0.5%. This calculation does not identify where loss occurred: source emission, transport, queue, parsing and storage must be distinguished. Record sequence identifiers to make that investigation possible.

### Correct, restore and regress deliberately

A defect record should state requirement, baseline, reproducible stimulus, expected and actual result, raw evidence, consequence and disposition. Severity follows the failed function and risk, not the number of affected configuration lines. A one-line permissive write rule can be more consequential than a large harmless inventory discrepancy. A failed test must remain linked to its correction and retest. Do not overwrite the original failure with the final successful screenshot.

After correcting a narrow defect, rerun the failed test and the adjacent functions that the correction could affect. Removing a broad rule should be followed by the intended permitted read, forbidden write and required emergency or failover conditions where relevant. A firmware change can justify wider regression than a documented rule-order correction. The selection needs an impact argument, not a fixed rule that always repeats either one test or the entire campaign.

Verify cleanup and restored authority. Remove temporary debug accounts and test exceptions, confirm active rather than merely saved configuration, check required monitoring, and retain a known recovery artifact. If the restore procedure reintroduces an exposed credential, configuration equality is not restored trust. Stop the campaign when required local control, protective independence, instrumentation or scope assumptions are lost. Resume only after the responsible authority establishes acceptable conditions and a revised plan. Factory testing should reveal failures without normalizing uncontrolled changes as part of troubleshooting.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.scenario: SYNTHETIC CASE — Isolated factory test CF22 uses gateway G and controller simulator C; no physical outputs are connected. Required behavior: support role R may read but never write; bad-quality or age-over-5 s samples inhibit supervisory writes. Active policy P11 is first-match: rule 10 permits R any application operation; rule 20 denies R writes. Candidate P12 reverses these rules. API transport returns HTTP 200, but the commit job reports failed: validation dependency missing; active policy remains P11. Session S1 was established under P11 before this attempt. Read TREAD succeeds. Write TWRITE receives a queue-accepted response, but independent simulated achieved state does not change. After a separate corrected commit, a fresh R write is denied, while S1 remains active under the fixture’s documented existing-session behavior. Data fixture: now=100.0 s, sample_time=99.0 s, quality=bad, cached_value=22.5; another sample_time=101.0 s, quality=good. Capture K sees no TWRITE packets but filters VLAN 31 while the actual test path is VLAN 30. Source emits 1,000 uniquely numbered alarms; 995 reach storage after the complete allowed interval, with collector drop counter increasing. A debug account remains enabled after restore, and the old restored backup contains a previously exposed support token.
worked_examples.solution:
The first forbidden write must be evaluated against P11: its broad first rule matches before the write deny. P12’s file contents do not fix that because the job failed and active state never changed. Preserve the validation failure, repair the missing dependency within the approved scope, commit and verify the active revision before retesting. For the later corrected state, test a fresh session and the pre-existing S1 separately; the supplied fixture behavior permits an old session to survive, so immediate authority withdrawal is not established by the new-session denial alone.

TWRITE’s queue acknowledgment is not completion evidence. The independent achieved-state result shows the required effect did not occur, although this observation by itself does not identify why. The 99 s sample is recent but bad quality, so the gate must reject it; the 101 s sample is future-dated under the shared time model and is also rejected. Capture K cannot support a claim of absent VLAN 30 traffic. Five alarm records remain missing, or 0.5%; the rising collector drop counter is a specific lead, not proof that every loss occurred at the same stage. Restore is incomplete while the debug account remains and the exposed token remains valid. Correct authority and monitoring, then regress the affected functions.

guided_practice.prompt: Write a diagnosis table separating the active-policy fault, session-lifecycle behavior, sample-quality failure, capture limitation and alarm-loss evidence. Evaluate both sample records with the supplied gate.
guided_practice.hint: Follow the actual transaction through effective policy and state. Separate a new request from an old authorized session and distinguish observations from hypotheses.
guided_practice.solution: P11 shadows its write deny; P12 was not activated because the commit job failed. Fresh-session denial after correction does not revoke S1. Both samples are unusable: one has bad quality and the other negative age. Capture K observes the wrong VLAN. Five missing unique alarms represent 0.5% of the generated set, with collector loss requiring focused investigation. Final closure also needs debug-account removal, exposed-token rotation and functional regression.

lessons.title: CSAT: prove site identity, physical mappings and end-to-end security integration
lessons.body:
### Identify what changes when the fixture reaches the site

A cybersecurity site acceptance test evaluates the installed integration, including dependencies that a factory fixture substituted or did not contain. Begin with a difference register: hardware identities, software and configuration revisions, addresses and routing, physical ports, directory groups, certificate trust, time sources, monitoring destinations, recovery infrastructure and physical point mappings. A factory pass remains useful evidence for its tested mechanism, but each relevant site difference requires an applicability decision and, where needed, a new test. Repeating an unchanged factory login demonstration does not validate a new site identity provider.

Compare approved design, delivered configuration and actual installed state. A rack label identifies intended placement; device serial, interface identity and verified cable termination establish the installed object. A reused address can point to a different server. An old hostname can resolve to a retired management service. A successful connection therefore needs target identity as well as reachability. Certificate-name failure after address reuse may be the control working correctly against an unintended endpoint, rather than a reason to disable validation.

### Trace the complete measurement chain

For a process measurement, record the physical variable and instrument, terminal and channel, controller I/O object, internal engineering variable, protocol object, gateway transformation, application point, display, alarm and historical record. Each edge can be wrong while every individual component remains healthy. A gateway returning 25.0 °C does not prove that the value belongs to the supply-water sensor the display names. A plausible return-water value can travel through a perfect network and still mislead a cooling decision.

Validate identity through an approved, independently observed stimulus or comparison. In an isolated fixture, vary the modeled supply input while keeping return constant and trace the raw value through every mapping stage. In a real installation, the qualified commissioning plan must define the permitted stimulus, expected process effect, instrument method and authority. The learner’s analytical result is not authorization to force a live I/O point, bypass an interlock or disturb a protective circuit. Review a proposed method and its evidence, and obtain supervised execution where physical work is required.

Address conventions matter. A displayed register label may be one-based while a protocol request uses a zero-based offset; an application may also use a vendor-specific reference notation. Record both the documented object and the actual request address. Do not globally add or subtract one from every point without verifying the device and client convention. A one-register displacement can return a plausible neighboring value, so reachability and normal-range checks are weak validators. Read-only interrogation of the approved object map in a representative fixture is a safer diagnostic first step than changing a live controller map.

Data representation is part of the interface contract. Specify width, signedness, byte order within a word, word order across a multiword value, scale, offset and invalid sentinels. For an unsigned 32-bit example whose high word is 0x0000 and low word is 0x09C4, the integer is 2,500. With scale 0.01 °C per count and zero offset, the engineering value is 25.00 °C. Swapping words would produce a very different number; applying the wrong scale can create a believable but incorrect one. For a signed 16-bit example, 0xFF9C represents -100 in two’s complement because 65,436 - 65,536 = -100. At 0.01 units/count, the result is -1.00 units, not 654.36.

Multiword consistency also matters. If the source updates words between separate reads, the client can combine halves from different values. Use the supported coherent-read mechanism or documented consistency indication. The right endian conversion cannot repair a torn sample. Preserve quality and source age through the gateway: successful polling of a cache does not reset the physical measurement’s acquisition time. A normal-looking interpolated trend across a source outage must not be presented as proof of valid measurement throughout the gap.

### Integrate identity, trust, time and observation

Check effective directory authority, including nested groups and retained assignments. A site maintenance user can inherit administrator rights even when its new access request says read-only. Exercise a permitted diagnostic operation and a relevant forbidden engineering operation using the actual site path. Include supported identity-provider loss and emergency access conditions where the requirement calls for them. Factory local-account tests cannot establish directory failure handling, cached authority or the new account’s complete effective scope.

Validate trust through the intended names, certificate chains, validity, key custody and renewal process. Different services can use different trust stores. A browser login succeeding does not show that an unattended agent trusts the same endpoint or that a future renewal reaches its store. Inventory certificate consumers and test the supported replacement workflow in a representative environment before relying on it in service. Do not replace a trust failure with permanent verification bypass and call that integration complete.

Time has both correctness and uncertainty. An event at 12:00:00 ±2 s has a possible interval from 11:59:58 to 12:00:02. Another at 12:00:03 ±2 s spans 12:00:01 to 12:00:05. These intervals overlap; the displayed three-second difference does not prove their order. Record clock source and uncertainty when correlating authentication, firewall and process events. For freshness tests, use the specified timestamp basis and handle synchronization loss explicitly. A negative calculated age after a clock step must not silently create an indefinitely fresh value.

### Exercise the installed end-to-end function

Alarm acceptance spans source condition, rule evaluation, alarm state, transport, notification service, intended recipient, acknowledgment and escalation. A server accepting a request does not prove the current duty person received it. Test approved synthetic conditions through the actual notification integration, avoiding real process disruption. Preserve event identity so the operator can link the notification to the originating asset and condition. Verify restoration and acknowledgment behavior as well as the initial alarm.

Installed redundancy requires a dependency inspection. Two labeled network paths may share a switch, power source, cable route or management authority. A factory link failure cannot prove independence from a site power supply that feeds both gateway control circuits. Trace actual dependencies and test only the approved failure domains using qualified authority. Also examine the alternate forwarding path: restored connectivity that bypasses the required security control is an availability recovery with a failed security invariant.

Close site acceptance with a reconciled as-built baseline and a list of residual deviations tied to requirements, consequences, owners and decisions. A supplier cannot convert an untested field dependency into a passed result by attaching the earlier factory report. Preserve required local control and protective independence throughout commissioning. Site evidence must establish both useful service and the intended security boundary under the accepted operating and failure conditions.

worked_examples.title: Worked engineering case
worked_examples.scenario: SYNTHETIC CASE — Site case S23: factory F7 used local users, a local clock and simulated I/O. The installed gateway now uses site directory D and time source N. Required supply-temperature point ST should represent supply sensor S on AI6, but the live map connects ST to AI7, whose verified wiring is return sensor R. Protocol fixture: unsigned 32-bit high-word-first words [0x0000, 0x09C4], scale 0.01 °C/count, zero offset; separate signed-16 differential point raw 0xFF9C, scale 0.01 units/count. Device documentation labels register 40021 while the selected client expects zero-based offset 20. Multiword value can change between separate word reads unless the supported coherent request is used. Event A timestamp=12:00:00 ±2 s; B=12:00:03 ±2 s. Hostname mgmt.example resolves to a retired server whose certificate name does not match. User maint7 inherits an administrator group from an older assignment. An alarm request is accepted by the notification server, but its destination is a retired mailbox. Network A and B have different switches; both gateway control-power feeds use site supply SP. The planned alternate route around failed firewall F uses router U without equivalent policy. Factory report P12/M8 is supplied, while the installed point map is M9. All numeric and protocol observations here are synthetic; no physical stimulus is authorized.
worked_examples.solution:
The unsigned value is 0×65,536 + 2,500 = 2,500 counts and therefore 25.00 °C. The signed point is 65,436 - 65,536 = -100 counts, or -1.00 units. These correct conversions do not fix the ST identity error: AI7 is return sensor R while the required source is S on AI6. Resolve the approved mapping and trace a bounded independent fixture stimulus or qualified field test through the complete chain. The selected register convention uses offset 20 for displayed 40021; do not apply a second decrement or assume every other client uses the same convention.

A spans 11:59:58–12:00:02 and B spans 12:00:01–12:00:05; their overlap prevents a definite event-order conclusion. Directory inheritance, retired DNS destination and retired alarm mailbox each require separate integration correction and tests. Distinct switches do not remove the shared SP power dependency. Router U restores an alternate path but violates the required policy boundary unless an equivalent approved control is demonstrated. M9 is a changed baseline, so factory mapping evidence must be assessed and the affected points retested rather than copied unchanged into site acceptance.

guided_practice.prompt: Produce a site-difference and verification table for S23. Decode the two raw values, trace ST’s identity defect, and calculate the event uncertainty intervals. Distinguish a network-path pass from power independence and policy preservation.
guided_practice.hint: Correct arithmetic can coexist with a wrong physical source. Consider which factory substitutes became real site dependencies.
guided_practice.solution: The values decode to 25.00 °C and -1.00 units, but ST is attached to the return rather than supply source. Use the supported address and coherent-read contract. The event intervals overlap from 12:00:01 through 12:00:02. Test actual directory roles, intended endpoint trust, duty notification and point mapping. Inspect the SP common dependency and reject the unmediated alternate route as equivalent security acceptance. Link the resulting tests to installed M9 and retain the factory result only within its applicable scope.

independent_task.brief: Write an installed-interface acceptance specification for one cooling measurement, one EPMS status and one remote maintenance path. Include protocol representation, physical/logical identity, quality/time, authorization, alarming and the boundary between analytical work and qualified field execution.
